key_insight: A small tetragonal distortion in BaTiO3 nanoparticles, stabilized by size and bonding control, can markedly boost ferroelectric polarization and piezoelectric output in lead-free nanogenerators.
engineering_relevance: This work shows that tuning nanoparticle crystallography and interface chemistry can improve self-powered device performance for wearable and low-power electronics.
method: Ligand-assisted sol-gel synthesis of BaTiO3 nanoparticles
Structural/chemical verification with XRD, Raman, and PDF analysis
DFT to probe Ti-O covalency, band gap, and dipole coherence
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~100 V open-circuit voltage and ~29 µJ energy storage for BTO-900, while BTO-1200 reached ~649 µW cm-2 power density and ~181 µA short-circuit current.
watch_item: Performance depends on nanoparticle size, tetragonal distortion, and interfacial charge trapping, so device optimization may not transfer directly across processing conditions or packaging formats.
paper_title: Small Distortions, Big Polarization: Tetragonal BaTiO3 Nanoparticles for High-Performance Piezoelectric Nanogenerators
